lines.title: Most prompts don't need a frontier model. Semantic Router dot net sends each one to the cheapest model that can answer it: a local model, your Claude subscription, or a paid API.
lines.install: Setup takes about a minute. Install it as a dot net tool.
lines.init: Then run in-it. It finds what's already on your machine. Here, that's L M Studio with two local models, and the Claude Code C L I you're signed in to. It writes a configuration with a capability tier for each model.
lines.start: Start the router. It speaks the OpenAI and Anthropic APIs, and prints exactly how to connect.
lines.connect: In a second terminal, point Claude Code at it with two environment variables. Claude Code works exactly as before. The router just decides which model answers each turn.
lines.hello: A simple question goes to a small local model. It's free, and it never leaves your machine.
lines.code: A small coding task goes to the local coder model.
lines.hard: A hard debugging question goes to Claude, where your subscription is worth spending.
lines.limit: And when you hit your Claude session limit, the router cools Claude down and keeps you working on local models. You don't change a thing.
lines.dashboard: The dashboard shows every decision as it happens: which route matched, which model answered, and how much stayed on your machine. Any OpenAI or Anthropic client can use the same endpoint.
lines.end: Semantic Router dot net. Open source, and MIT licensed. Install it with one command, and stop paying frontier prices for small prompts.
